text:
maya: Heads-up — running into weirdness with canary experiments in Console. Canary traffic is 5% but we've seen it get spike-throttled by customer quotas and then variant metrics look wrong. Anyone else?
sam: saw this. Rate limits / quota enforcement happen at the routing layer today (per-api-key token). If canary splits are just tagging requests, quota calc still counts them against the key.
eli: yep. This causes "canary undercount" where variant latency looks fine but throughput collapses because quota errors (429) are routed fallback to baseline. :grimacing: 
maya: Can we make canary buckets exempt from soft rate limits or have separate quota windows? Thinking about two options: (A) ephemeral canary tokens with separate quota envelope, (B) route canary to dedicated pool that has its own rate-limiter. Thoughts?
loren: product POV — prefer (B) — less surprising to customers and easier for billing. But we need telemetry to show split-level consumption.
sam: Ops: (B) is doable but adds infra. Quick compromise: add a header-based guard that marks canary requests and applies a lenient soft-limiter but still counts them for billing. Example config idea: 
```yaml
routing:
  match: header(x-redwood-canary) == "1"
  rate_limit:
    soft: 0 # disabled
    hard: 10000/min # safety cap
  billing: count
```
eli: important: ensure quota enforcement still protects noisy tenants — cannot create unbounded exposure. Hard limit is must.
maya: on telemetry: we need per-variant QPS, 429 rate, and downstream latency buckets in Console. Right now dashboards are per-route only.
loren: added to roadmap but we need a short-term panel. @eli can you add a per-variant counter and a minimal Grafana view? Capture: variant_id, outcome (ok/429/500), latency_ms.
eli: will do, but it's a few hours. Also propose we instrument experiment_id & variant_id in the access logs so we can join.
maya: agree. Also need UX in Console to show "canary health" with green/yellow/red based on 429 ratio > 1% or latency+error delta > 20%.
sam: note: watch out for split behavior when fallback policy routes 429 -> baseline — baseline variant gets extra weight artificially. We should track original target variant in telemetry even after fallback.
deploy-bot: deploy started for rollout-service v3.14.0 — routing header rollout flags -> new limiter behavior.
maya: ok, action items: eli add telemetry counters + logs, sam design limiter config change + safety docs, loren update Console panel & health criteria. I'll open a PR for the docs.
